title: Successor step in the left external cup coefficient bound
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X,Y$ quasi-compact $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme] with affine diagonals, and $F,G$ quasi-coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Use the scalar resolution models [lem-sc-picard-kunneth-resolution-model] and normalization [lem-sc-picard-external-cup-cochain]. Write $H^p$ for module right-derived global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Fix $G$ and $d\in\mathbb N$. Suppose that for every quasi-coherent $F\prime$ with $H^p(X,F\prime)=0$ whenever $d<p$, every normalized realization has invertible homology in every natural degree. If $H^p(X,F)=0$ whenever $d+1<p$, then every normalized realization for $(F,G)$ has invertible homology in every natural degree.

source.place: Varieties Tag 0BED proof after equation 33.29.1.1: exact coefficient sequences, two dimension-shifting inductions and acyclic Leray base case

proof.text: Equip X with its specified k-structure f and transfer the affine-diagonal instance. Use the existing quasi-coherent acyclic embedding theorem to obtain a mono i:F -> E, with E quasi-coherent and H^p(E)=0 for 1<=p. Construct Q as the categorical cokernel of i. Existing cokernel closure proves Q quasi-coherent; the canonical cokernel sequence S=(F -> E -> Q) is short exact.

Apply the full long exact sequence of right derived global sections to S. For d<p, natural-number arithmetic gives 1<=p and d+1<p+1. In the exact segment H^p(E) -> H^p(Q) -> H^(p+1)(F) both outer objects are zero, so H^p(Q) is zero. Acyclicity likewise gives the bound-d vanishing of E. This only needs exactness; no separate dimension-shifting isomorphism or vanishing of H^0(Q) is assumed.

Choose normalized cochain realizations cE and cQ using the existing cochain existence theorem. Invoke the given bound-d induction hypothesis with the bounds just proved, giving homology isomorphisms for cE and cQ in every natural degree.

Apply the short exact left coefficient homology-ladder theorem to S, cE, cQ and the specified c. Its two outer-invertibility implications give isomorphisms at positions 0,1,3,4. Apply Mathlib's five lemma to its two exact rows and phi, giving IsIso at position 2. The central comparison equality rewrites H(c) as e1.inv followed by phi_2 followed by e2.hom, a composite of isomorphisms. This proves the original conclusion in degree n.

proof_origin.place: E2: Tag 0BED, one left-coefficient successor step. Lean proves acyclic embedding/cokernel assembly, the lower cohomological bounds from the full derived long exact sequence, the applications of ih, the five lemma, and central isomorphism transport. The geometric ladder is isolated in lem-sc-picard-external-cup-left-homology-ladder.

lean.statement:
theorem picardExternalCupCochain_isIso_shiftLeft
    (k : Type w) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{w})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [CompactSpace Y]
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal f)] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal g)]
    (G : Y.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] (d : ℕ)
    (ih : ∀ (F' : X.Modules) [F'.IsQuasicoherent],
      (∀ p : ℕ, d < p →
        IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj F')) →
      ∀ (c' : picardExternalTotal f g F' G ⟶
        picardScalarModel (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) (externalCupCoefficients f g F' G)),
        IsPicardExternalCupCochain f g F' G c' → ∀ n : ℕ,
          IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap c' (n : ℤ)))
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : ∀ p : ℕ, d + 1 < p →
      IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj F))
    (c : picardExternalTotal f g F G ⟶
      picardScalarModel (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) (externalCupCoefficients f g F G))
    (hc : IsPicardExternalCupCochain f g F G c) (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap c (n : ℤ))
